name: Inkface Blockfolk
oneLine: Classic R6 block bodies with rounded heads and flat black-ink sticker faces: solid oval eyes, thick brows, red open mouths, one expression per shot, a signature colour on the lead.
head: Rounded classic block head (Cast v2 head='classic'), 25% of body height without hair, width 0.62 of torso; matte plastic skin, roughness 0.5
face: Flat vector decal in ink #111111, no nose, no 3D features, line weight 3-4% of head width; blush hatch #F59BB0, tears #6EC3F4, stubble dots on adult men; face scale fs 0.80-0.86 so it reads full-body
eyes: Solid black vertical ovals 9% x 14% of head size, centres +-13% from the midline at 45% height; variants: happy up-arc with lashes, sad or sleepy down-arc, shocked inverted V, squeezed > <; thick tapered brows angled +-20-25 deg for anger or fear; terror variant: white sclera ovals with a black outline and small pupils (the only time whites appear)
mouth: Centre at 70% height: dash, closed arc, smug hook, open D filled red #D7262B with pink tongue #F06A6A, black ring with red inside (shock), white gritted-teeth rectangle with 3 lines, zigzag (scared), small o

proportions.limbs: R6 boxes: arms and legs 1x2x1 (half the torso width, as long as the torso), hands the same width as the arm

bodyTypes: kid (scale 0.85; the source uses the same size)
baby (head 45% of height, framed in a cradle)
creature or big thing 1.5-2x adult height, pale or desaturated, or a different material (porcelain, carved wood with drawn eyes, bark)
hair: Chunky low-poly shards (8-14 spikes or locks), flat saturated colour, no strands, +30-40% head height, overhangs the sides 10-15%, fringe to the brows; long hair is a solid sheet with a side fringe; palette #F56E02 #7A4A2A #E8C25A #1E1A1A #B8B4B0 #A63A1E
clothing: Base shirt and trousers plus one 3D layer (vest, apron, jacket, knit); the most textured surface on screen (cable knit, denim, worn leather, fleece; bump 0.18-0.30); one dominant colour per person; the lead's signature colour is unique
accessories: Big readable props: hats and helmets, satchels, lanterns, wooden swords, crowns, staves, ropes, keys, chest plates or sashes that carry the story rule; magic items emissive magenta #E722BD or ember #E35214
materials: Plastic skin and hair (roughness 0.5), fabric() clothing with bump, low-roughness metal, emissive magic; no outlines on geometry, ink only in the face decal; one motivated key light, no fill
motion: Held readable poses (arms out 'what?!', pointing, sitting, lying, cowering); plain game walks (about 1 step per 0.5 s) and ragdoll tumbles; no lip sync, no blinks, faces change only on cuts; offset crowd idles; the camera carries the motion
recipe: person(name, shirt, pants, skin, face, hair, head='classic') with the R6 defaults tw=2.0 td=1.0 th=2.0 lh=2.0 lw=1.0 aw=1.0 al=2.0 hs=1.0
Size with the root scale s: adult 1.0, kid 0.85, little kid 0.62, big guard 1.05 with tw=2.4
Draw 8-10 expression PNGs (1024x1024, transparent) with flat black shapes per the face spec; save to /tmp/claude-0/cast2/faces/face_<name>_<expr>.png; use head_mat2(..., fs=0.80-0.86)
Skin from the skinTones list via srgb(); roughness 0.5
Hair: an existing hair_col key, tint_hair(key, rgb) from the hair palette, hair_s 0.95-1.05 so it overhangs 10-15%
Clothing: fabric(name, rgb, sc) plus one 3D layer box() in knit, denim or leather (bump 0.25 for knit)
Give only the lead the signature colour; check everyone else against it
Accessories with the box, cone, torus and ball helpers; emissive via mat(emit=..., estr=5-8)
Pose with the R6 pivots (arms=, out=); add breathing (torso Z +-1%, 3 s) and offset idles
Render a cast-check still under ember-interior and moon-night lighting at phone size and push it per the Studio Bible
